name: Background tab timer throttling
plain: Hidden tabs get slower timers: 1 per second, then 1 per minute after 5 minutes in Chrome.
meaning: Tells the site whether the tab is visible and caps how much it can do while hidden. Useful for battery, but sites also detect tab switches via visibilitychange.

web.api: document.visibilityState, visibilitychange; setTimeout/setInterval; Page Lifecycle freeze/resume

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: Chrome aligns timers to 1 s; after 5 min with chained timers it runs them once per minute
Page can be frozen then discarded

limits.headline: Can't keep its timers running fast once you switch to another tab
limits.user_action: You switch to another tab or app and leave the page.
can: Run its code once a second while the tab is hidden
Keep playing sound, if the page plays audio
Slow down by itself to save battery
cannot: Keep fast timers in a hidden tab; they drop to once a second, then once a minute after 5 minutes in Chrome
Stay running as normal after you lock your phone
Turn off the browser's own power saving limit
Do heavy work in the background without a background task such as a worker or a service worker

story.what_it_is: When a tab is hidden, the browser slows its clocks to save battery.

marketing.name: Timer throttling in Chrome 88
marketing.pitch: Chrome explains that background tabs get less frequent timers, to save power and CPU.

story.for_you: You switch away from a tab and your laptop fan stays quiet. The cost is that some live things, like a countdown or a game, may lag or stall until you return.
story.for_makers: Makers must design around it: pause animations, use server time, and keep calls and live connections alive for real time apps. Browsers use it to keep ads and trackers from burning battery.

use_cases.example: An idle game or a browser multiplayer game must handle the tab being frozen, or it drops you from the match.
A live auction or sports score page catches up with the server when you return to its tab.
A video call tab keeps audio running even when hidden, because audio is allowed to play.
Ad measurement counts a view only when the tab is visible, so hidden tabs do not inflate numbers.
A web chat app uses a push connection so it notifies you even when throttled.
Time on page tools pause counting when the tab is hidden.

technical_bounds: Chrome 57: budget based throttling; hidden timers wake about once per second
Chrome 88 intensive throttling: after 5 min hidden, timer chains of 5 or more run once per minute (page silent 30 s, not using WebRTC or audio)
Exempt: audible tabs, active WebRTC data channels or media streams, pages with Web Locks or IndexedDB transactions in flight
requestAnimationFrame pauses completely in hidden tabs; Safari throttles to 1 s then suspends; Firefox clamps to 1 s (and 10 s in some setups)
Memory Saver (Chrome 108+) can discard inactive tabs; wasDiscarded reveals prior discard

history.change: Intensive wake up throttling after 5 minutes hidden
Page Lifecycle API with freeze and resume
